q: In a high-end condominium unit, which finish or fixture would be the least expected choice?
o: Engineered wood flooring in the bedrooms
n: Luxury units are specified with split-type or centralized air conditioning for quieter operation and a cleaner facade; a window-type unit is a budget solution tied to entry-level projects, not high-end ones.

q: If a condo unit has only one window, which space should ideally sit beside it?
n: When a compact unit has only one source of natural light and ventilation, that opening is prioritized for the bedroom, since occupants spend extended hours there and need daylight and air circulation most directly.

q: Elevator sizing and specification for a high-rise residential project is influenced by all of these EXCEPT:
o: The target travel speed of the car
The total number of floors served
The overall height of the building
The projected population of the building
n: Elevator sizing and specification are driven by traffic-design inputs — building height, population, floors served, and target car speed. "PSOmax" is not a recognized elevator traffic-design parameter, so it is the one item that does not factor in.

q: Which use pairs best with high-rise residential floors in a mixed-use building?
n: Retail and commercial space is the classic podium use paired with residential towers — it activates the ground levels and serves residents without the noise, traffic, or operating-hour conflicts of office, industrial, institutional, or school uses — per standard mixed-use planning practice in the source document.

q: Under the Fire Code, all of these must be located in the fire command center EXCEPT:
o: Controls to simultaneously unlock stairway doors
Fire detection and alarm annunciator panel
All of the items above belong in the fire command center
Sprinkler valve and water-flow display panels
n: The fire command center consolidates the alarm annunciator, sprinkler/water-flow monitoring, voice communication system, and stairway door-release controls in one place for staff to monitor and operate during an emergency — none of the listed items is excluded — per RA 9514, Fire Code of the Philippines.

q: In a low-end or economically priced condominium, which amenity would be least likely to appear?
n: Entry-level projects typically economize on individual unit fit-out and rely on window-type units instead; split-type air conditioning is the step up associated with mid- to high-end projects, even though shared amenities like a pool or lobby are still commonly provided.

q: Just past the front door of a studio-type condo unit, which area is typically encountered first?
n: In the typical studio layout, the kitchen sits nearest the entry so wet, service-heavy activities stay close to the plumbing stack and away from the sleeping and living zones at the far end of the unit.

q: Under RA 9514, which of these is NOT required in every building classified as high-rise?
o: All of the above are required in every high-rise building
n: Sprinklers, smoke control in protected spaces, and fire-rated stair enclosures are baseline life-safety requirements applied across high-rise buildings, but a dedicated fire command center is only mandated once a building crosses additional height/occupancy thresholds — per RA 9514, Fire Code of the Philippines.

q: Which kitchen configuration is most common in a studio condo unit?
o: Any of these — it varies by owner
n: A studio unit's limited floor area normally reduces the kitchen to a single run of counter and cabinetry along one wall, the layout that uses the least floor space among standard kitchen configurations.

q: Which statement correctly describes good practice for laying out a high-rise condominium floor plate?
o: The unit depth (long dimension) should stay constant across unit types
Larger units (2BR, 3BR) should be positioned at the building corners
Both the constant-width principle and the corner-placement principle apply
The unit width (short dimension) should stay constant across unit types
Both the constant-depth principle and the corner-placement principle apply
n: Standard condo-planning practice keeps unit depth uniform across the floor plate so the structural grid and envelope repeat efficiently, varying only the frontage width, with premium larger units placed at corners to capture two exposures.
